description: CGV-3 People management: add/edit/verify/remove people with photo from camera or gallery via expo-image-picker, multipart photo upload, one person markable as is_caregiver, rendered with the shared PersonCard. Backend people module is a STUB (404 until PPL-2); build the full UI wired to the contract and note the stub. Installs the expo-image-picker native package. Depends on FEAT-001. Independent of FEATs 002, 004, 005.
steps: Read context.json and this FEAT file FIRST.
From mobile/ install the picker: `npx expo install expo-image-picker` (NOT npm i, so an SDK-52-compatible version is chosen). It will add the dep to package.json.
Rebuild app/(caregiver)/people.tsx: list via listPeople() from src/api/people, rendered with the shared PersonCard (pass hubUrl from getHubUrl() so photo_path resolves). loading/error/empty states.

Add/Edit form (inline modal or pushed route) with fields: name (required), nickname, relationship (required), notes (multiline), and an is_caregiver toggle. Enforce that at most one person is the caregiver: when enabling is_caregiver on one person, clear it on any other via updatePerson(otherId, { is_caregiver: 0 }). Send SQLite booleans as 1|0.

Photo: request permissions and let the caregiver pick from camera (ImagePicker.launchCameraAsync) or gallery (ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync). From the picked asset build an UploadFile { uri, name, type } (derive name/type from the asset; default type 'image/jpeg') and call uploadPersonPhoto(id, file) AFTER the person exists — create the person first (createPerson), then upload the photo to the returned id.
Create via createPerson(input: PersonInput), edit via updatePerson(id, input), remove via deletePerson(id) with a confirm Alert.
Add a verify action that sets trust via updatePerson(id, { trust: 'verified' }).
Add an inline code comment that the people backend is a stub (routes 404 until PPL-2) and the screen is wired to the documented contract.
acceptance_criteria: A person can be added with name, nickname, relationship, notes and a photo picked from camera or gallery, with the photo uploaded via uploadPersonPhoto (multipart).
Exactly one person can be marked is_caregiver; enabling it on one clears it on others.
People are listed using PersonCard with photos resolved from the hub URL.
Edit, verify (trust='verified'), and remove (with confirm) all work via updatePerson/deletePerson.
expo-image-picker is installed via `npx expo install` and appears in package.json.
From mobile/: npm install succeeds, npx tsc --noEmit prints zero errors, and grep -rn 'fetch(' app returns nothing.
findings: Rebuilt app/(caregiver)/people.tsx (replaced the Placeholder) as a list + inline Modal Add/Edit form. List renders via listPeople() using the shared PersonCard with hubUrl from getHubUrl(); loading/error/empty states follow the project pattern (ApiError message + retry). Form fields: name (required), nickname, relationship (required), notes (multiline) and an is_caregiver Switch. 'At most one caregiver' is enforced on save by clearing is_caregiver (updatePerson(otherId,{is_caregiver:0})) on every OTHER person carrying the flag; SQLite booleans are sent as 1|0. Photo via expo-image-picker: requestCameraPermissionsAsync + launchCameraAsync and requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync + launchImageLibraryAsync (mediaTypes ['images']); the picked asset becomes UploadFile {uri,name,type} with name/type derived from asset.fileName/asset.mimeType, defaulting type to image/jpeg, and is uploaded via uploadPersonPhoto(id,file) AFTER the person exists (createPerson first on add, then upload to the returned id). Create=createPerson, edit=updatePerson, remove=deletePerson behind a confirm Alert, verify=updatePerson(id,{trust:'verified'}). All network I/O goes through src/api/people and src/api/client (no raw fetch). Added an inline comment that the people backend is a stub (routes 404 until PPL-2) and the screen is wired to the documented contract. Installed expo-image-picker ~16.0.6 via `npx expo install` (now in package.json). Build gate PASSED from mobile/: npm install exit 0, npx tsc --noEmit zero errors, grep -rn 'fetch(' app returns nothing. On-device/Expo Go boot and live calls against the stubbed people backend were NOT run here.
